skill.displayName: Pet Grooming Effectiveness & Hairball Risk Analysis | 宠物梳毛器梳理效果与毛球风险

llm.summary: This pet grooming analysis skill is mostly coherent, but it silently creates or reuses cloud-linked identity state and stores tokens while uploading user media to remote services.

dimensions.detail: Network upload of media is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the skill reads workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt as an identity source, sends identity and platform metadata to external services, and may fetch user-supplied URLs server-side without clear confirmation or URL scoping.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer script or executable file mode was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though one requirements file names yaml==6.0.3 rather than PyYAML, which may be an installation bug rather than a security issue.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for or reveal identity parameters, auto-triggers history queries, and hides --open-id/--api-key from CLI help; this is partially documented as internal behavior, but it reduces user control over account-linked cloud queries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The shared common library creates a workspace data SQLite database and can persist user records with token and open_token fields; this persistence is not clearly bounded to the grooming workflow or clearly explained to users.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core media analysis, report links, and history lookup match the stated grooming-analysis purpose, but the implementation also performs automatic identity resolution, remote login/registration, token handling, and local account persistence that are higher impact than a user would expect from simple pet image/video analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this skill only if you are comfortable with uploaded pet photos/videos or submitted URLs being processed by lifeemergence.com services, with cloud history tied to an internally generated or reused identity, and with local storage of account tokens in the workspace data directory. Avoid using private household images or sensitive URLs unless the service's retention and access controls are acceptable to you.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr filters are in a local generic DAO helper; they are a code quality and robustness issue, but I did not find evidence that this path exposes arbitrary code execution or drives the final verdict.
[LP3] unexpected: The manifest describes server-side API calls and local files, but it does not clearly disclose the full local identity-file, token persistence, and remote login/registration behavior, so the least-privilege concern is supported in part.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The hidden --open-id path, workspace identity-file reuse, automatic default-user creation, remote /sys/phoneLogin call, and token storage are artifact-backed and materially broaden the skill beyond straightforward media analysis.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The CLI suppresses identity arguments while the code consumes them and the instructions say not to expose identity handling to the user; this is not necessarily malicious, but it is under-disclosed account-context handling.
[SDI-1] expected: History-report listing and report export URLs are documented in SKILL.md, so they are not hidden, but they remain sensitive because they expose account-linked prior analysis records via cloud APIs.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger language defaults to running when media is provided for analysis and history queries auto-trigger on keywords; because uploads and account-linked cloud queries occur, explicit user confirmation would be safer.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media processing is stated in the description, but the artifact does not prominently explain identity metadata, token transmission, automatic registration, or persistence, so several privacy concerns remain valid.
[E1] unexpected: The POST to the health-service login endpoint sends openId/mobile-derived identity data and can silently register/login users; this is not sufficiently explained as part of pet grooming analysis.
